findings.where: The full-width blue band right under the hero, 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform' with its white Subscribe button (desktop-02 top; phone-01, where the heading runs to three lines at the hero's size)
findings.fault: A second call to action sits straight under the first screen. It is a saturated full-bleed blue field, which makes it the loudest thing on the page, louder than the hero's own address button. It offers a briefing subscription the brief never mentions and that Mark may not run. It speaks of 'Mark' in the third person and in a sales register ('Get …'). Its link goes to #subscribe, and no subscribe section exists on the page, so the button leads nowhere.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brief asks for one message and one action and bans salesy copy and invented offers. Mark, because the personal-advisor test needs his first-person voice. A bank officer who clicks Subscribe and gets nothing will trust the site less.

findings.fault: The first screen has no navigation, only the name and the logo. A visitor has no route to his articles, talks, CV or a Contact label. The palette table even assigns a colour to 'nav links' that the page never shows.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brief lists nav as part of the first screen exactly as a visitor sees it. A procurement reader looking for his work or CV has nowhere to go but the email.

findings.where: Article specimen: the body paragraphs, the subhead's lead-in and the three-item numbered list (desktop-04, -05, -06; phone-03, -04)
findings.fault: The long reading text is centre-aligned. Every line starts at a different point, so the eye has to hunt for the next line. The numbered items are centred too, so the numbers sit far from their own text and at a different gap on each item. The title, meta line and image above them are left-aligned, so the column has no single edge.
findings.who_objects: Readers of Mark's articles, who must read paragraph after paragraph with ragged left edges. Angélique, whose lists will always look broken. The founder, because the article specimen is meant to be the product.

findings.fault: The direction is 'Mark at work', a full-bleed photo of him speaking. What shows is a keyed-out head and shoulders floating very large on slate. The lectern and the event are gone, and the hair edge shows the cut-out. It reads as an oversized cut-out portrait, not a man at work, and the face rivals the heading for first attention.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for a photo of Mark speaking that sets the scene, with his line over the calm side. The floating cut-out loses the 'at work' proof and looks less refined.

findings.where: Hero top-left lockup: 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the MMM Infra mark
findings.fault: The name is set small and light, while the white arches beside it are bigger and heavier. The logo wins the lockup, and the name does not lead.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brief says his name leads, with the logo beside it.

findings.where: The lecture card at the end of the article specimen ('Streamlining the PPP Process…', PDF)
findings.fault: The card has a download icon and a 'PDF' label, but its link goes to #article, an anchor on the page, not a file. A visitor expecting the lecture download gets nothing.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants to take the lecture away. The research calls the PDF list 'the product', so a link that promises a download and does not deliver one breaks that trust.

findings.fault: The card stacks a blue border, a blue tint fill and a wide soft shadow. Nothing else on the page is raised, so it reads as a promotional box dropped into a quiet editorial page.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for a refined, unsalesy look. The house surface rules allow one separator, not a strong border with a strong fill and a shadow on one resting element.

findings.where: The 'PALETTE' section label, and the blue numbers in the article's list
findings.fault: Text that cannot be clicked is set in the link blue. The page's own note says 'blue only where something can be clicked', so the blue label and numbers look like links.
findings.who_objects: Readers, who learn on this page that blue means 'click' and then find blue text that does nothing. The house link rule keeps the link colour for links.

findings.where: The section labels below the fold: 'PALETTE', 'Type pair', 'Texture', 'An article page', 'Motion sketch'
findings.fault: Five labels of one kind get three treatments. 'PALETTE' is blue tracked capitals, which the type note itself forbids. 'Texture' is a large italic serif. The rest are small bold grey sans.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the tile, since like parts treated unlike makes the system look unsettled and contradicts its own type rules.

findings.where: First screen: what sits beside the action
findings.fault: Nothing beside the email action proves the work: no named body, region, recent talk or date. The newest lecture (23 April 2026) is buried at the end of the article specimen.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer deciding whether to write. Before getting in touch, they need to see that he has done this work for bodies like theirs, in their region.

findings.where: Palette text-pair table at phone width (phone-02)
findings.fault: The contrast ratio '11.66 : 1' breaks across two lines, and the pair names wrap awkwardly around their 'Aa' chips.
findings.who_objects: The founder reading the tile on a phone, who sees a broken figure in a specimen meant to show care.
